title: Characteristics of patients attending a consultation for temoporomandibular dysfunction (TMD) at a university clinic
summary:
Background:
About 10 % of the population experience pain in the jaw joints, the chewing muscles, or surrounding areas. These problems are often not immediately recognized as dental issues. As a result, affected individuals frequently visit several doctors or therapists before the true cause is identified.
Study Aim:
The study examines which patients visit the CMD clinic at MHH, why they come, and what difficulties they have experienced in diagnosis and treatment in the past. In addition, the study looks at how effective specific conservative treatments are for the patients.
Methods:
Patients undergo a clinical examination and complete questionnaires regarding their symptoms and quality of life. After six months, the examination is repeated to document any changes under therapy.

interventions.name:
Clinical diagnosis for TMD patients according to DGFDT + completion of a questionnaire to collect demographic data, reasons for referral, preliminary diagnosis, and previous treatment + completion of the OHIP-G14
Follow-up after six months: repeat clinical examination + OHIP G14 to evaluate changes

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients presenting for TMD diagnostic at the clinic of Prosthetic Dentistry and Biomedical Materials Science.
Exclusion criteria:
-Psychological limitations that prevent understanding of the questionnaire, the study, or giving informed consent
-Refusal to participate in the study
-Lack of capacity to provide informed consent
